title: Local balances dashboard
outcome: Running the app locally (pnpm run dev) and opening the page shows every account SimpleFin returns for the configured SIMPLEFIN_ACCESS_URL, grouped by institution, with each account's current balance and currency. The access URL/credential never reaches the browser.

included: Next.js (App Router, TypeScript) app scaffolded in this repo, joined to the js/ pnpm workspace, with working lint/typecheck/test/build scripts and scripts/verify-task.sh wired to them
A server-side route handler that reads SIMPLEFIN_ACCESS_URL from a server-side-only env var and calls SimpleFin's /accounts endpoint, returning a balances-only JSON shape to the client
A single dashboard page fetching from the app's own API route and rendering accounts grouped by institution/org, with balance, currency, and as-of date, plus clear loading and error states
Tests and manual verification run against SimpleFin's public demo bridge, never a real linked account
excluded: Any deployment target (Vercel, etc.) -- local dev only
Multi-user auth or any login system
Using or requesting Adam's real SimpleFin access URL for any orchestrator task or verification step

behaviors.description: With SIMPLEFIN_ACCESS_URL pointed at SimpleFin's public demo bridge, running pnpm run dev and loading the page shows the demo accounts grouped by institution, each with a balance and currency.

While loading the page, the browser's network tab shows no request whose URL, headers, or body contains the SimpleFin access URL or its embedded credential; the API route's response body also never contains it.
With SIMPLEFIN_ACCESS_URL unset, loading the page shows a clear error state instead of an unhandled crash or a blank page.
If SimpleFin's API returns an auth error or is unreachable, the dashboard shows a clear error state instead of an unhandled crash or a silently empty account list.
